welcome.label: Welcome · the lost time capsule

parts.label: 🕳 Six holes
parts.title: Nobody found it
parts.body: Six people followed the map. Six holes. No time capsule.

parts.label: 🔍 Today
parts.title: Describe how things move
parts.body: Where it started, where it ended, and which way it went.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a folded paper like a treasure map.) I have a treasure map. Want to see?

[ON SCREEN: Teo’s map]
Teo buried a time capsule on the beach. Start at the rowboat, walk five steps, dig. Easy, right?

[ON SCREEN: Six holes]
Six people tried it. Six holes. Nothing. Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: Today]
Today you’ll learn how to describe motion so clearly that nobody gets lost. Read Teo’s map, just below me, and see what you notice.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · which train moved? (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🪧 The station sign
parts.title: Something that stays put
parts.body: It never moves. So it can tell you who did.

warmup.script:
(Sit very still. Slowly slide your hand past your face like a train going by.) Whoa. Am I moving, or is that train moving?

[ON SCREEN: Which train moved?]
Press Watch and look out the left window. Then vote. Did your train move, or the other one? It is okay to say you can’t tell yet.

[ON SCREEN: The station sign]
Then look out the right window and find the station sign. Take both trips. The second one might fool you!

part1.label: Part 1 · find it from the clue (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Point to your desk, then count three hand-steps to the right.) My pencil is three hands to the right of my mug. Can you picture it?

[ON SCREEN: Find it from the clue]
Read each clue. Find the thing it starts from, count the steps and tap that square. North is up on this map. Watch out for the last clue. It was written yesterday.

part2.label: Part 2 · program the helper (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🤖 Meet Scoot
parts.title: Scoot does exactly what you say

part2.script:
(Close your eyes. Take four small steps in a random direction, then open them and look surprised.) Four steps! Did I end up in the right place?

[ON SCREEN: Meet Scoot]
Scoot is Sam’s delivery robot. Tap an arrow card, set the steps, and press Go.

[ON SCREEN: The order slip]
The first slip only says four steps. What is missing? Fix it. After three deliveries, a surprise is waiting.

[ON SCREEN: The Ferris wheel]
If you get off a Ferris wheel right where you got on, did you move? Vote, then ride.

explore.label: Part 3 · diagram the replay (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Roll a pencil or a toy car across your desk. Stop it. Point to where it started, then where it ended.) It started here. It ended there. It went that way.

[ON SCREEN: A sample diagram]
A motion diagram is a picture of that. Start, end, an arrow, and a reference point: the tree.

[ON SCREEN: Diagram the replay]
Your turn. Watch a crab and a seagull. Plant the Start flag and the End flag, name the direction and the path, then tap something that stays put. Your description writes itself.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What is wrong with Teo’s directions?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to work
rows: Draw and label your own motion diagram

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. So what is wrong with Teo’s directions, and what would fix them? Pick the answer that fits every clue. Then help Scoot dig up the capsule.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
After that: two short answers. Then watch something move at home, like a toy car or your pet, and draw its motion diagram. Label the start, the end, the direction and your reference point. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “You can describe motion without a reference point. Just say how far it moved.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Hold up five fingers.) It moved five steps. There. Do you know where it is now?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says how far is all you need. Think about the train window, and Scoot’s slip that only said four steps.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🗺 Your specimen
parts.title: Teo’s treasure map
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next lesson
parts.title: How fast did it move?
parts.body: Distance and time tell us speed.

closing.script:
(Hold up the folded map again.) Start at the lamp post. Five steps east. Three steps south. Dig! Now THAT is a map.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and Teo’s map goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Bonus: the compass]
Want more? Try the compass at the very end, and the Night Delivery game.

[ON SCREEN: Next lesson]
Next time: we know which way it went. But how fast?

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
